editorials.titleTr: Special Insurrection Investigative Unit: Politics, Pure and Simple
summaryTr: The presidential office is reviewing the establishment of a special task force dedicated to investigating the December 3rd illegal martial law.
The formation of a new organization amid ongoing investigations has raised suspicions of political motives.
Prioritizing the special task force without institutional reforms risks lowering investigative quality and sparking political controversy.
editorials.bodyTr: The presidential office is considering establishing a special investigation headquarters for sedition to probe those involved in the illegal martial law declared on December 3. Officials have discussed beginning with police and expanding the operation once the newly launched Serious Crimes Investigation Agency is launched. With investigations into sedition already proceeding vigorously through multiple special prosecutors and task forces, the new dedicated organization has raised suspicions of political motives. Experts have pointed out that if the government prioritizes establishing a special headquarters over institutional reform amid changes to the criminal justice system, it will result in deteriorating investigative quality and intensifying political controversy.

editorials.titleTr: U.S. Treasury Yields Show No Signs of Slowing; Brace for Fallout Ahead
summaryTr: U.S. Treasury yields hit their highest levels in decades.
Rising oil prices and expectations of rate hikes triggered a sell-off in government bonds.
High interest rates are putting pressure on Korean bonds, loans, and exchange rates across the board.
editorials.bodyTr: U.S. Treasury yields have reached their highest levels in decades for both 10-year and 30-year bonds, increasing financial uncertainty worldwide. Rising oil prices stemming from the re-escalation of U.S.-Iran tensions, combined with expectations of further rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, have driven increased selling of government bonds. As surging Treasury yields push up Korean bond rates, borrowing costs, and exchange rate pressures, the government, corporations, and households must prepare for elevated interest rates as a constant reality.

editorial.body: 입력 종합 30면 어제(28일) 군 당국은 지난 21일 발생한 서부전선 비무장지대(DMZ) 내 폭발사고의 원인이 목함지뢰와 유사한 북한의 반보병지뢰에 의한 것일 가능성이 높다고 밝혔다. 사고 발생 후 7일 만이다. 2025년 9월 북한이 인근 지역에 지뢰를 매설한 흔적이 있는 점, 작전에 참여했던 장병 다수의 증언, 폭발 화염의 형태와 피해 장병의 부상 정도, 국립과학수사연구원에 의뢰한 장병들의 피복 및 장구류, 화약류 채취 거즈 등에 대한 폭약 성분 감정 결과 등을 바탕으로 이런 결론을 내렸다고 한다. 일단 사고 원인에 대한 가닥이 잡혔지만, 이번 사고 대응 과정에서 보인 군 당국의 태도는 국민의 공분을 사고 있다. 군 당국은 현장 훼손을 막기 위해선 신속한 현장 조사가 필요함에도 사고 발생 8일 만인 29일 현장 조사를 하려다 여론의 질책을 받자 이틀 당겨 27일에야 착수했다. 그마저 안전상 이유로 현장 접근조차 하지 못했다. 사고 직후, 작전 참여 장병들이 폭발한 2개 외에 추가로 미폭발 지뢰 한 발이 있었다고 증언했는데 아직도 이를 수거하지 못하고 있다. 더 큰 문제는 2024년 북한 김정은 국무위원장의 ‘적대적 두 국가론’ 천명과 이에 따른 ‘국경선 요새화’(3중 철책 설치 및 지뢰지대 조성) 지시 이후 지난해 9월 이번 사고 현장 인근에서 북한군의 지뢰 매설 동향이 관측됐는데도 적절한 대응을 하지 않았다는 점이다. 군사분계선(MDL) 이남 지역의 지뢰 매설은 명백한 정전협정 위반이다. 그런데 군은 1년이 지난 후에야 뒤늦게 수색작전에 나선 것이다. 이와 관련, 일각에선 전임 사단장이 합참으로부터 현장을 확인하고 북한군의 작업 동향을 직접 관찰하라는 지시에 소극적으로 대응했다는 의혹이 제기되고 있다. 해당 사단장은 이후 군단장으로 진급했으나 얼마 전 ‘빈총 경계’ 지침으로 직무 배제된 상태다. 또 정부는 출범 이후 DMZ 관할권을 놓고 유엔군사령부와 갈등을 빚어 왔다. 이 때문에 북한군의 지뢰 매설과 관련한 업무 협조가 원활하게 이뤄지지 못한 것이 아닌지도 따져볼 일이다. 강신철 국방부 장관은 어제 늑장 대응 비판에 “일부러 늦게 하거나 은폐하는 것은 분명히 없다”며 “합당한 상응 조치를 하겠다”고 했다. 강 장관의 공언대로 정부는 북한의 지뢰 매설을 강력 규탄하고 사과와 원상 복구, 재발 방지 요구 등을 통해 책임을 물어야 한다. 또한 또 다른 MDL 이남 지역에 북한군이 지뢰를 매설하지 않았는지도 철저하게 조사해야 한다. 국경선을 지키는 것은 안보의 기본 중 기본이다. 지금 국민은 우리 장병의 희생에 대해 군이 얼마나 엄중하게 대응하는지를 지켜보고 있다.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] DMZ Blast Likely North Korean Act...Violates Armistice, Demands Stern Response
summaryTr: DMZ explosion confirmed as North Korean mine attack...military authorities determine cause in 7 days
Military's sluggish response leaves North Korean mines unattended for a year even after observations of mine-laying in September 2024
Government must condemn North Korea and demand apology while conducting comprehensive mine resurvey across entire DMZ
editorial.bodyTr: Military authorities announced yesterday that the explosion that occurred in the Demilitarized Zone along the western front on the 21st was likely caused by North Korean anti-personnel mines similar to coffin mines. This conclusion came seven days after the accident. The military based this determination on evidence including North Korea's mine-laying activity observed in September 2025 in the vicinity, testimony from numerous soldiers who participated in the operation, the shape of the explosion flames and the degree of injuries sustained by affected soldiers, and results from forensic analysis of soldiers' uniforms, equipment, and explosive residue collected on gauze that were submitted to the National Forensic Service. While the cause of the accident has been identified, the military authorities' response to the incident is drawing public criticism. Although a swift on-site investigation was necessary to prevent tampering with the scene, the military authorities initially planned to conduct the investigation on the 29th, eight days after the accident. Only after facing public backlash did they move up the timeline and begin on the 27th, two days earlier. Even then, they could not access the site due to safety concerns. Immediately after the accident, soldiers who participated in the operation testified that there was one unexploded mine in addition to the two that detonated, yet it has not been recovered. The greater problem is that despite observing North Korean military mine-laying activity near the accident site in September last year following North Korea's declaration of "hostile two-state theory" by Chairman Kim Jong-un in 2024 and subsequent orders to "fortify the border" through the installation of triple barriers and mine fields, the military took no appropriate measures. Mine-laying south of the Military Demarcation Line is a clear violation of the armistice agreement. Yet the military only launched search operations a year later. Some have raised suspicions that the former division commander responded passively to orders from the Joint Chiefs of Staff to confirm the site and directly observe North Korean military operations. That division commander was later promoted to corps commander but has since been removed from duty under the "unloaded rifle" alert directive. Additionally, the government has been in conflict with the United Nations Command over jurisdiction of the DMZ since taking office. This raises questions about whether smooth cooperation regarding North Korean mine-laying operations has been hindered. Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said yesterday in response to criticism of the delayed response that there was "clearly no intentional delay or cover-up" and pledged to "take appropriate corresponding measures." As Minister Kang promised, the government must strongly condemn North Korea's mine-laying, demand an apology, restoration, and prevention of recurrence, and hold them accountable. Furthermore, a thorough investigation must be conducted to determine whether North Korean troops have laid mines in other areas south of the MDL. Defending the border is fundamental to national security. The public is now watching how seriously the military responds to the sacrifice of our soldiers.

editorial.title: Why the delay?
editorial.body: The military drags its feet in on-site probe after a mine blast in DMZ injures 3 soldiers South Korea’s military and the UN Command investigated the site of a suspected land mine explosion in the western part of the Demilitarized Zone on Sunday, six days after the incident happened. The military initially said it would investigate the site on Tuesday, after the Chuseok holiday, citing the risk of a secondary explosion during the investigation. Amid growing controversy over the delay and concerns of evidence being destroyed, however, it moved up the investigation by two days. The military authorities said the investigation team failed to reach the point of the explosion due to the high risk posed by unidentified mines in the area and the extreme fatigue of personnel involved in the operation. As a result, key questions, including possible North Korean military involvement, remain unanswered, fueling suspicions and criticism of the military authorities. The military bears much of the responsibility for the controversy, having failed to respond actively from the outset. At a Defense Ministry briefing the day after the accident, a Joint Chiefs of Staff official repeatedly responded to a barrage of questions with “We’ll check.” The explosion left two service members seriously injured, one of whom suffered an ankle amputation, while another was lightly injured. Yet the military later inexplicably excluded the lightly injured service member from its injury count, raising suspicions that it was deliberately downplaying the accident. The military did not begin preparatory checks on the environment near access to the site until Saturday, five days after the accident and a day before the planned investigation. Security and safety concerns may justify withholding information or delaying entry into an accident site, but it is difficult to justify taking five days merely to prepare for an investigation. Opposition allegations of a deliberate delay cannot be dismissed. Rep. Han Dong-hoon, an independent lawmaker, alleged that the military obstructed the investigation by rejecting the UN Command’s request for an immediate joint investigation. The Joint Chiefs of Staff said that the site was too dangerous and that ensuring investigators’ safety and conducting a rehearsal had to come first. But if the operation was so dangerous, sending troops into the area without adequate preparation in the first place was itself the problem. In 2015, during the conservative administration of President Park Geun-hye, North Korean wooden-box mines exploded in the Demilitarized Zone. In that case, the military collected mine fragments from the site on the day of the incident and began a joint on-site investigation with the UN Command two days later. This was not because the front line was somehow safe at the time. While the military delayed the on-site investigation, citing the Chuseok holiday and safety concerns, the area was hit by heavy rain. Opposition lawmakers called attention to the rain forecast, but the military did not move up the on-site investigation. Evidence that could help determine the cause of the explosion may have been washed away. In the most recent incident, South Korean troops were injured when suspected mines exploded while they were clearing a search route to determine whether North Korean soldiers had crossed the Military Demarcation Line and laid mines on the South Korean side. North Korean troops had been observed laying mines near the MDL for several months. Criticism is mounting that the failure to act on those warning signs may have contributed to the accident. In serious incidents like this, an early investigation is crucial. However, the military did not begin its on-site investigation until almost a week after the incident. It is also difficult to understand why the military says access to the site of the explosion was difficult when troops had already been there. The military’s passive response stands in contrast to its handling of the 2015 wooden-box mine provocation. It must be made clear, beyond any doubt, why the military dragged its feet on the on-site investigation. 지연된 수사는 은폐 의혹을 불러일으켰으며 폭우로 인해 중요 증거가 파괴될 가능성을 열어두었다.
비판자들은 군의 완만한 대응이 이전 행정부 당시의 더 신속한 조사와 대조된다고 지적한다.
editorial.bodyTr:
군부, DMZ 지뢰 폭발로 군인 3명 부상 후 현장 조사 질질 끌어

한국군과 유엔군사령부는 지난일요일 비무장지대 서부지역의 의심되는 지뢰 폭발 현장을 조사했다. 사건 발생 6일이 지난 후였다. 군은 당초 추석 휴일 이후인 화요일에 현장 조사를 진행하겠다고 밝혔는데, 조사 과정에서 2차 폭발 위험을 이유로 들었다. 하지만 지연에 대한 논란이 커지고 증거 훼손 우려가 제기되자 조사를 이틀 앞당겼다. 군 당국은 조사팀이 지역 내 미확인 지뢰로 인한 높은 위험성과 작전에 투입된 인원의 극심한 피로를 이유로 폭발 지점에 도달하지 못했다고 설명했다. 결과적으로 북한군의 가능한 관여 여부를 포함한 핵심 질문들은 미해결 상태로 남았고, 이는 의심과 군 당국에 대한 비판을 키웠다.

군부가 처음부터 능동적으로 대응하지 못한 점이 이번 논란의 상당 부분을 차지한다. 사건 다음날 국방부 브리핑에서 합참 관계자는 쏟아지는 질문들에 "확인하겠습니다"라는 답변을 반복했다. 폭발로 인해 두 명의 군인이 중상을 입었는데, 이 중 한 명은 발목 절단을 당했고 다른 한 명은 경상을 입었다. 그런데 군은 이후 경상을 입은 군인을 부상자 수에서 제외시켜 사건을 의도적으로 축소하려는 것 아니냐는 의혹을 낳았다. 군은 사건 발생 5일째 되는 토요일, 즉 예정된 조사 하루 전에야 현장 접근로 근처 환경에 대한 사전 점검을 시작했다. 보안과 안전 문제가 정보 공개를 유보하거나 사건 현장 진입을 지연시킬 수 있는 정당한 사유가 될 수 있지만, 단순한 조사 준비만으로 5일을 소비한 것을 정당화하기는 어렵다. 야권이 주장하는 의도적 지연이라는 지적을 완전히 배제할 수 없다.

무소속 한동훈 의원은 군이 유엔사의 즉시 합동 조사 요청을 거부해 조사를 방해했다고 주장했다. 합참은 현장이 너무 위험하며 조사인원의 안전 확보와 사전 리허설이 우선되어야 한다고 설명했다. 하지만 작전이 그렇게 위험했다면, 처음부터 충분한 준비 없이 부대를 그 지역에 투입한 것 자체가 문제다. 2015년 박근혜 보수 정부 당시 비무장지대에서 북한의 나무상자 지뢰가 폭발했다. 당시 군은 사건 당일 현장에서 지뢰 파편을 수집했고 2일 후 유엔사와 함께 현장 합동 조사를 시작했다. 이는 당시 전선이 어떤 방식으로든 안전했기 때문이 아니었다. 군이 추석 휴일과 안전 문제를 이유로 현장 조사를 지연하는 동안 해당 지역에 폭우가 내렸다. 야권 의원들이 강우 예보에 주목했지만, 군은 현장 조사를 앞당기지 않았다. 폭발의 원인을 규명하는 데 도움이 될 수 있는 증거들이 빗물에 씻겨 내려갔을 수 있다.

이번 사건에서 남한 군인들은 북한군이 군사분계선을 넘어 남한 지역에 지뢰를 설치했는지 여부를 판단하기 위해 수색 경로를 개척하던 중 의심되는 지뢰가 폭발해 부상을 입었다. 북한군은 수개월간 군사분계선 근처에서 지뢰를 설치하는 모습이 포착되었다. 이러한 경고 신호에 대응하지 못한 것이 사건 발생에 기여했을 가능성이 있다는 비판이 커지고 있다. 이러한 심각한 사건에서는 신속한 조사가 매우 중요하다. 그러나 군은 사건 발생 거의 일주일 후에야 현장 조사를 시작했다. 또한 부대 인원들이 이미 그 현장에 있었는데 폭발 지점에 접근하기 어려웠다는 군의 설명도 이해하기 어렵다. 군의 수동적 대응은 2015년 나무상자 지뢰 도발 당시의 대응과 대조를 이룬다. 군이 현장 조사를 질질 끈 이유가 무엇인지 의심의 여지 없이 명확히 해야 한다.

합참, DMZ 폭발은 북한 지뢰가 원인으로 보인다고 발표

한국 합동참모본부는 지난주 비무장지대 내에서 군 인원 3명에게 부상을 입힌 폭발은 북한이 원인일 가능성이 높다고 월요일 밝혔다.

editorials.title: Why the delay?
editorials.body: The military drags its feet in on-site probe after a mine blast in DMZ injures 3 soldiers South Korea’s military and the UN Command investigated the site of a suspected land mine explosion in the western part of the Demilitarized Zone on Sunday, six days after the incident happened. The military initially said it would investigate the site on Tuesday, after the Chuseok holiday, citing the risk of a secondary explosion during the investigation. Amid growing controversy over the delay and concerns of evidence being destroyed, however, it moved up the investigation by two days. The military authorities said the investigation team failed to reach the point of the explosion due to the high risk posed by unidentified mines in the area and the extreme fatigue of personnel involved in the operation. As a result, key questions, including possible North Korean military involvement, remain unanswered, fueling suspicions and criticism of the military authorities. The military bears much of the responsibility for the controversy, having failed to respond actively from the outset. At a Defense Ministry briefing the day after the accident, a Joint Chiefs of Staff official repeatedly responded to a barrage of questions with “We’ll check.” The explosion left two service members seriously injured, one of whom suffered an ankle amputation, while another was lightly injured. Yet the military later inexplicably excluded the lightly injured service member from its injury count, raising suspicions that it was deliberately downplaying the accident. The military did not begin preparatory checks on the environment near access to the site until Saturday, five days after the accident and a day before the planned investigation. Security and safety concerns may justify withholding information or delaying entry into an accident site, but it is difficult to justify taking five days merely to prepare for an investigation. Opposition allegations of a deliberate delay cannot be dismissed. Rep. Han Dong-hoon, an independent lawmaker, alleged that the military obstructed the investigation by rejecting the UN Command’s request for an immediate joint investigation. The Joint Chiefs of Staff said that the site was too dangerous and that ensuring investigators’ safety and conducting a rehearsal had to come first. But if the operation was so dangerous, sending troops into the area without adequate preparation in the first place was itself the problem. In 2015, during the conservative administration of President Park Geun-hye, North Korean wooden-box mines exploded in the Demilitarized Zone. In that case, the military collected mine fragments from the site on the day of the incident and began a joint on-site investigation with the UN Command two days later. This was not because the front line was somehow safe at the time. While the military delayed the on-site investigation, citing the Chuseok holiday and safety concerns, the area was hit by heavy rain. Opposition lawmakers called attention to the rain forecast, but the military did not move up the on-site investigation. Evidence that could help determine the cause of the explosion may have been washed away. In the most recent incident, South Korean troops were injured when suspected mines exploded while they were clearing a search route to determine whether North Korean soldiers had crossed the Military Demarcation Line and laid mines on the South Korean side. North Korean troops had been observed laying mines near the MDL for several months. Criticism is mounting that the failure to act on those warning signs may have contributed to the accident. In serious incidents like this, an early investigation is crucial. However, the military did not begin its on-site investigation until almost a week after the incident. It is also difficult to understand why the military says access to the site of the explosion was difficult when troops had already been there. The military’s passive response stands in contrast to its handling of the 2015 wooden-box mine provocation. It must be made clear, beyond any doubt, why the military dragged its feet on the on-site investigation. editorials.titleTr: When Money Runs Out, Limits of Gyeonggi Province Youth Basic Income Come to Light
summaryTr: Gyeonggi Province's youth basic income has hit a financial crisis.
The province decided to drastically reduce its budget burden from 70 percent to 30 percent.
The structure is being shifted to pass a 70 percent share of costs to municipal governments.
editorials.bodyTr: Gyeonggi Province's youth basic income has hit a wall of fiscal reality. The province decided to completely adjust the funding ratio for the youth basic income project starting next year, shifting from "70% provincial funds and 30% municipal funds" this year to "30% provincial funds and 70% municipal funds." The province has essentially offloaded its burden onto municipalities. Youth basic income is a universal welfare policy introduced in 2019 when President Lee Jae-myeong served as Gyeonggi governor. Regardless of income level, it provides 24-year-olds with regular cash payments. The project, which began as a pilot program in some areas, has now expanded to all municipalities in the province, with the number of beneficiaries continuously growing. The fiscal burden has consequently ballooned. Last year, the provincial government spent 1.34 trillion won on youth basic income, and this year's budget is expected to reach 1.7 trillion won. The province's finances are already stretched thin due to increased social welfare spending, infrastructure investments, and other commitments. Unable to shoulder the growing burden alone, the province is now attempting to transfer the financial responsibility to municipalities. However, this creates an unfair situation where municipal governments must find ways to cover the increased costs. This approach is problematic because it essentially abandons the provincial government's responsibility for a policy it championed. If the province lacks fiscal capacity, it should reconsider the program's scale or seek alternative funding sources rather than simply passing the burden downward. The youth basic income program deserves support as a forward-looking welfare initiative, but it cannot be sustained through financially irresponsible measures. A more rational and equitable funding framework must be established.

국제 정세 변화 속에서 위기관리의 중요성이 더욱 높아졌다.
한국은 전략적 대응으로 국익을 지켜야 한다.
editorials.stance: 미중 경쟁 시대에 한국의 전략적 위기관리 능력 강화를 촉구하는 입장
editorials.titleTr: Trump Checkmate Fails as China's Influence Grows...Crisis Management Now More Crucial [Editorial]
summaryTr: China's influence continues to grow despite efforts to counter Trump.

South Korea must protect its national interests through strategic response.
